Based on submitted therapy screens and nursing flow sheets, the member's current baseline demonstrates significant limitations in physical stamina and sustained attention. Treating physician may request peer-to-peer discussion within standard timeframes. Standard appeal rights initiated per CMS guidelines.

Reviewing Medical Director: Dr. Patrick Ewing, MD

I conducted a peer-to-peer discussion with the attending practitioner at Lakeshore Care Centre regarding the request for short-term skilled nursing facility (SNF) coverage for Mr. Thompson.

As a preliminary note, the facility submitted comprehensive clinical records, physician orders, and therapy evaluations. This determination is not based on any deficiency in documentation, as all required clinical materials were fully furnished and reviewed prior to our conversation.

During the call, the attending physician reviewed the member's recent change in functional status and requested skilled physical and occupational therapy services. In evaluating the member's clinical presentation, substantial consideration was given to the member's established history as a long-stay resident at Lakeshore Care Centre, where he has resided at a custodial level of care for several months. The chronic functional deficits and medical complexities that originally necessitated long-term nursing home placement reflect an established baseline of extensive dependency. The requested interventions, while beneficial to the member's general well-being, align with ongoing maintenance care rather than an intensive, short-term skilled rehabilitative program requiring daily skilled management. Because the member's current care requirements are consistent with the chronic baseline needs associated with his prolonged custodial placement, skilled nursing facility admission under the Medicare Advantage benefit cannot be certified.

The initial adverse determination is therefore upheld. Alternate supportive measures and continued restorative nursing programs within the current custodial setting were discussed with the attending physician.

Member Name: Dirk Nowitzki
Member ID: SYN-313151
Health Plan: Harborview Medicare Plus
Facility: Birchwood Nursing and Rehabilitation
Reviewing Official: Dr. Bill Russell, Medical Director
Date of Determination: May 18, 2026

DECISION: UPHELD

The Independent Review Entity has completed its reconsideration review of the coverage determination issued by Harborview Medicare Plus. Based on our clinical assessment of the submitted medical record, the plan's denial of short-term Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) coverage is hereby upheld.

BACKGROUND CONTEXT
Medical records indicate that the member has maintained an extended custodial residence at Birchwood Nursing and Rehabilitation prior to the acute change in condition. Please be advised that this decision is based solely on current clinical presentation; the member's long-term residency history does not serve as a basis for this denial.

CLINICAL RATIONALE
Following documentation review concerning the recent change in health status, the requested daily skilled level of care is not supported. The interventions currently outlined in the treatment plan do not inherently require the continuous, specialized expertise or administration of a licensed professional nurse or licensed therapist. Furthermore, the documented clinical needs—consisting primarily of functional assistance, routine observation, and medication management—do not demonstrate a severity requiring seven-day-a-week skilled nursing or five-day-a-week skilled rehabilitation services. Because these services do not necessitate daily licensed professional oversight and can be safely delivered via non-skilled supportive care, the criteria for Medicare SNF benefit coverage are not satisfied.

Dr. Bill Russell, Medical Director
Independent Review Organization

Member Name: Kawhi Leonard
Member ID: SYN-112961
Requesting Provider: Riverside Manor
Requested Service: Short-Term Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) Stay
Date of Determination: November 12, 2026

NOTICE OF COVERAGE DETERMINATION
Summit Ridge Advantage HMO-POS has completed its review of the prior authorization request submitted on your behalf for skilled nursing facility coverage at Riverside Manor. Coverage for this request has been denied.

WHY DID WE DENY THE REQUEST?
Under the provisions of your Summit Ridge Advantage HMO-POS plan, skilled nursing facility benefits must be rendered by a contracted, in-network facility. Riverside Manor is not an active, participating provider within the Summit Ridge Advantage HMO-POS network. Because Riverside Manor does not hold a contractual agreement with our plan for institutional skilled nursing services, the requested admission cannot be authorized for coverage under your plan benefits.

TRANSFER AND NETWORK OPTIONS
Your plan covers skilled nursing care when received at an approved network facility. If you wish to utilize your skilled nursing benefit, our care management team can coordinate with the staff at Riverside Manor to locate a participating in-network skilled nursing facility and arrange for an authorized transfer.

YOUR RIGHT TO APPEAL
If you believe this decision is incorrect, you, your authorized representative, or your treating physician have the right to appeal. You must submit your appeal request within 60 calendar days from the date of this letter. You may request a fast (expedited) appeal if your healthcare provider indicates that waiting for a standard review timeframe could seriously jeopardize your health.

Reviewed by:
Dr. Dikembe Mutombo, Medical Director
Utilization Management, Summit Ridge Advantage HMO-POS
